name: Fitness Tracker
highLevelGoals: The user aims to easily record and monitor various physical activities, such as running, walking, or cycling, to maintain a comprehensive log of their exercise habits.
The user seeks clear and intuitive visual representations of their activity data to easily monitor their fitness progress, identify trends, and stay motivated.
The user desires the ability to set, edit, and track personalized fitness goals (e.g., daily steps, calories burned) to provide clear targets and maintain focus on their fitness journey.
The user expects to receive personalized workout recommendations and plans based on their fitness level, preferences, and goals to maximize the effectiveness of their workouts.
The user aims for the application to connect and automatically sync data from their wearable devices to ensure accurate and up-to-date tracking of their fitness metrics.
The user wants to share their fitness activities, achievements, and progress on social media to engage with friends, celebrate milestones, and inspire others.
The wearable device aims to accurately collect and transmit fitness data, such as heart rate, steps, and calories burned, to the application in real-time.
The wearable device seeks to establish and maintain a stable connection with the fitness application to ensure continuous and uninterrupted data synchronization.
lowLevelGoals: The user can initiate the recording of a new physical activity (e.g., running, walking, cycling) within the application.
The user can choose the specific type of activity they are performing from a list of available options (e.g., 'Run', 'Walk', 'Cycle', 'Swim').
The user can manually enter or adjust details for an activity, such as its duration, distance covered, and estimated calories burned, if not automatically tracked.
The user can save the recorded details of a completed physical activity session to their activity log.
The user can access a chronological list or summary of all their previously recorded physical activities.
The user can view their daily activity metrics (e.g., steps, calories, active minutes) presented in a graphical chart format.
The user can view a line graph or bar chart showing their progress for a chosen metric (e.g., distance, average heart rate) over a week.
The user can apply filters to their activity history or visualizations to display data only for specific activity types (e.g., show only 'Running' activities).
The user can view a comparison of their current week's or month's activity data against a previous equivalent period to identify changes in performance.
The user can set preferences for receiving notifications when fitness milestones or goals are achieved.
The system automatically triggers and displays notifications to the user upon reaching fitness milestones or goals.
The user can define and add a new personalized fitness goal, specifying the metric, target value, and timeframe.
The user can modify the parameters (e.g., target value, deadline) of a previously set fitness goal.
The user can see a visual representation (e.g., progress bar, percentage) of how close they are to achieving their active fitness goals.
The user can manually mark a fitness goal as achieved once they have met its criteria.
The user is presented with a suggested workout plan or activity based on their profile and recent activity.
The user can adjust settings to receive workout suggestions that match their desired intensity (e.g., 'light', 'moderate', 'intense').
The user can browse and select from a collection of pre-designed workouts with instructions and demonstrations.
The user can rate or provide comments on the relevance and effectiveness of the suggested workouts to improve future recommendations.
The user can start the process of connecting their fitness application with a new wearable device.
The user can see which wearable devices are currently paired and connected to their fitness application.
The user can initiate a manual sync of data from their connected wearable device to the application.
The user can unpair or remove a previously connected wearable device from the application.
The user can post details of a specific completed activity (e.g., a run, a workout) to their chosen social media platforms.
The user can post an update or notification about achieving a specific fitness goal to their social media.
The user can control who sees their shared fitness activities and achievements on social media (e.g., public, friends only).
The user can link their fitness application profile to various social media platforms for easy sharing.
The wearable device continuously measures and records the user's heart rate.
The wearable device accurately tracks and counts the number of steps the user takes throughout the day.
The wearable device calculates an estimate of calories burned during physical activities and throughout the day.
The wearable device sends its collected fitness data to the connected fitness application.
The wearable device initiates and maintains a Bluetooth connection with the fitness application on the user's smartphone or tablet.
If the connection to the application is lost, the wearable device attempts to automatically reconnect without user intervention.
The wearable device provides a visual or haptic indicator to the user about its current connection status with the application.
